decisions.claim: On a real install the owner cannot traverse the 0770 mgmt directory, so --migrate and --destinations fail
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED, and proved the mechanism locally against /var/cache/cups (root:lp 0770) -> Permission denied. Deferred to the same change as F2, not because it is minor but because the obvious fix (usermod -aG wundervault) hands F2's re-key attack to every agent: agents run as the owner's uid, so any permission the owner has the agent has. Needs the owner's decision on the read side; see the question put to the user.

decisions.claim: register_profile accepts no setup token; B2/B3/check 7 unimplemented
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. registerProfile (agent.ts:200) overwrites an existing profile by name INCLUDING socket_token, so whoever reaches the mgmt socket can re-key an agent and read its credentials off the per-agent socket. Fix is an auth redesign spanning onboard.py in the burnbox repo; putting the shape to the owner before building it rather than guessing.

decisions.claim: Migration counts a name already known to the daemon as migrated and shreds the legacy store without comparing credentials
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED at migrate.ts:130 + the allIn check at :169. A daemon holding a stale profile for the same name causes the only good copy to be destroyed. Now compares before counting it across, and never shreds on a name-only match.

decisions.claim: Nothing disables the old systemctl --user unit (spec F2)
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED - it is running on this machine right now, and server.ts:108 deliberately falls back to its socket. Migration deleting the store does not stop it: it serves from memory. Now stopped and disabled as part of migration, and verified afterwards.

decisions.claim: Per-agent socket existence discloses which agent names are registered
decisions.reason: Partly confirmed. The refusal path is genuinely indistinguishable, but RuntimeDirectoryMode=0755 makes /run/wundervault world-listable, and ping returned the full agent list to any caller. The directory listing is inherent to per-name sockets and is accepted and now documented; the gratuitous disclosure via ping is removed.

decisions.claim: Knocks is a lockout, not a rate limit, and keeps answering
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED and WORSE than reported. lockedOut() is checked BEFORE the token is compared (agent.ts:245), and is keyed on the agent NAME, so ten bad tokens from any local process deny the legitimate agent its credentials for 60s - repeatable indefinitely. This phase introduced it by making the socket world-connectable. A valid token is now always served; the cost is moved onto the failing caller.

decisions.claim: Migration neither verifies nor repairs the mode of an existing token file
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED, with a second layer the reviewer did not name: writeFileSync's mode argument is ignored when the file already exists, so even the rewrite branch leaves a 0644 token at 0644. The same bug class is live today - ~/.wundervault/agents is 0775 because mkdirSync's mode was masked by umask. Both chmod'd unconditionally now.

decisions.claim: The installer accepts an ExecStart under /home, which ProtectHome=yes then hides
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED and fatal on this machine: wundervault-agent resolves to /home/zee/.local/bin/wundervault-agent. The install would have reached step 4 and failed with 203/EXEC. The installer now refuses a home-based path and says what to do instead.

decisions.claim: The daemon-absent migration test resolves the legacy store to the real home
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED - the test printed /home/zee/.wundervault/agent-profiles.enc. Only the ping-first ordering stops it shredding a live store. Exactly the accident that destroyed one before. The test now pins WUNDERVAULT_USER_ROOT into the scratch root and asserts the redirect took.

decisions.claim: The lockout is a denial-of-service against the legitimate agent
decisions.reason: Same defect as F6; fixed together.

decisions.claim: A decrypt failure leaves an empty store that the next save overwrites
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED at agent.ts:166-174: the catch logs and leaves this.profiles empty, and saveProfiles then writes a store containing only the newest profile. A recoverable key mismatch becomes total credential loss. The daemon now refuses to serve or save from a store it could not read.

decisions.claim: No test runs the installed unit with two real uids under the real systemd sandbox
decisions.reason: Correct, and it is the reason every one of these blockers survived 366 passing tests. A real two-uid install test is the next piece of work, but it needs the install to be performed on this machine first - which is the owner's call, not mine.

decisions.claim: Agent names and sockets are machine-global across multiple human users
decisions.reason: Real, but out of scope for this spec: the product targets one human per machine today and the spec's C5 already states one uid is one principal. Noted for the owner.
